attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his Substack post, written in his own voice. It is not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalisation keeps the force of 'just' and 'at all'. Dropping 'still' does not change the meaning much. It is a firm characterisation with no hedge, but it is essentially evaluative.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary. It keeps the strong denial and does not water it down. The contract rightly notes that 'conceptual depth' has no definition or test, so any verdict would depend on a criterion the speaker never supplied.

evidence.note: A 2016 textbook links depth to layered composition and to learned concept hierarchies. That bears on the terminology clause, but its technical sense of 'concepts' does not settle conceptual depth in Marcus's sense.
The 2022 KataGo adversarial paper documents one specific failure mode. It is relevant to Marcus's example but cannot establish a general absence of conceptual depth.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm but evaluative characterisation. 'Conceptual depth' has no stated definition, threshold or observable test. The textbook definition (e1) and the Go failure (e2) are context only: neither confirms nor refutes the substantive denial without adding a criterion the speaker did not give. The claim is untestable as stated, so it is not scored.
